shared.common: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: Kavriva KPSS academic category illustration, Batch 06 art-direction exploration only. Create ONE standalone square illustration, not a sheet, not UI, no typography or digits anywhere. Transparent background (true alpha). Center a clear compact composition occupying about 65% of the square, with generous quiet empty margin on all sides. Shared brand: premium modern calm academic technology product, dependable and structured, not childish. Exact primary accent direction #4F46E5 indigo, restrained pale indigo, white and cool light neutral supporting forms, dark ink #101828 for a few necessary details. Indigo is the main colored accent, no extra hue families. Maintain uncluttered hierarchy, broad readable shapes, rounded geometry consistent with a 24px/1.75px round cap outline UI icon family without turning this illustration into an icon. No logo, no Kavriva K mark, no wordmark, no slogans, no captions, no watermark, no random symbols of brands. No humans, no mascot, no Pixar, no neon, no stock photography, no textbook worksheets, no clutter, no rainbow gradients, no toy plastics, no emoji. All text labels will be added later as editable text outside the art. Preserve vector-friendly clear silhouette in raster form.

styles.a: Direction A — Geometric Editorial. Flat/soft-depth hybrid modern editorial SaaS illustration. Front-facing 2D geometric composition with very slight paper-like overlap and an extremely light soft shadow; NOT perspective/isometric. Three meaningful major forms maximum, clean solid fills, controlled indigo area, plenty of negative space. Timeless scalable geometry; crisp restrained rounded edges, thin consistent ink details, no complex micro-detail. Shared perspective frontal with small overlaps, ambient top-left light, very shallow depth.
styles.b: Direction B — Structured Isometric Lite. Restrained academic spatial composition, very light isometric at a consistent 30-degree angle. Structured low-profile objects with thin slab depth, clean matte finish, neutral diffuse lighting from upper-left, soft short contact shadows. Not full 3D, not photorealism, not plastic, not toy blocks. Three major forms max, broad surfaces and clear silhouette; muted white/neutral object surfaces with controlled indigo planes and sparse dark-ink edges. Same spatial language should work on a small mobile category card.
styles.c: Direction C — Abstract Data / Knowledge Visual. Frontal abstract knowledge-flow composition, gentle layered planes, connected diagram nodes and meaningful geometric routes. Human-independent intelligence/SaaS illustration, warm clarity rather than cold enterprise dashboard. Restrained thin round-ended connectors; pale neutral small panels and strong indigo anchor shapes. Centered radial-to-linear knowledge arrangement, only a handful of nodes, no literal UI screenshot, no tables, no numbers. Diagrammatic soft translucency limited to pale indigo overlapping planes, very shallow depth, no glowing neon.

subjects.CAT-01: Mathematics: analytical reasoning, problem solving, patterns, structure and logic. Use a resolved relationship between one indigo triangle, a balanced geometric construction/axis motif and a small set of aligned pattern tiles. It should read as spatial/analytical thinking, NOT a calculator, not a pile of digits, not a worksheet or formula poster.
subjects.CAT-03: History: chronology, causal relationships and accumulated structured knowledge. Use a compact archive-card stack and three ordered milestones connected along a calm timeline; one earlier layer leads into the next. No readable writing. Not a museum poster, antique parchment, a monument, Ottoman imagery, costume, map of an empire, military badge, or a generic history book.
subjects.CAT-04: Geography: spatial reasoning, regions, terrain and relationships. Use a small abstract regional contour/landform composition with three adjacent geographic areas and a clear directional/relational cue. The regions should suggest a designed terrain diagram, not a real country outline, not Google Maps, not a literal atlas, not a globe or map pin pile. No place names, scale numbers, legends or text.
